title: The sower again (Mark 4:1–20)
hookLine: now read the parable with the explanation beside it
tomorrow: the seed that grows while you sleep

lines: STORY AND EXPLANATION, SIDE BY SIDE.
cards: A farmer flinging seed: some on the path, some on rock, some in thorns, some on good soil. You've met him before, back in the stories camp, in Matthew's gospel. That time, it was a story.

Now, reading Mark straight through, he comes back in Mark's own words, and this time you can do what a good reader does: lay the story beside the explanation Jesus gives his friends afterward, and look closely at one kind of ground.

teach.b: First, the setting. The crowd is so big that Jesus gets into a boat and sits on the water, teaching the people on the shore. He begins, in the Douay-Rheims: "Hear ye: Behold, the sower went out to sow."
Four kinds of ground. Seed on the path is eaten by birds. Seed on rock springs up fast and withers in the sun, with no root.
Seed on good ground yields thirty, sixty, a hundredfold. And he ends: he that hath ears to hear, let him hear. Second, the explanation.
Later, alone with the twelve, Jesus explains it line by line. The seed is the word. The path is the person the word never gets into.

The rock is the one who welcomes it with joy but falls away when trouble comes. Good ground is the one who hears, receives, and bears fruit. Third, the thorns, and there's nothing dramatic about them.

"And the cares of the world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts after other things entering in choke the word, and it is made fruitless." The thorns don't kill the seed on the first day. It sprouts.
It's just slowly crowded out by worry, by money, by wanting other things, until nothing comes of it. Nobody decides to stop listening. It gets choked.
Thirty, sixty, a hundredfold: some readers hear that last number as astonishing to people who farmed.

teach.h: THE CARES OF THE WORLD CHOKE THE WORD.
teach.b: The parable ends not in failure but in abundance.

how: Catholics hear the parable of the sower at Sunday Mass in Ordinary Time, and some use it for lectio divina, asking which kind of ground they are right now.

o: a new parable about a second planting season
the parable of four grounds, read again in Mark
a farmer who has to sow his field twice

games.q: what's inside the parable — tap the pairs.
p: joy, then falls away in trouble

s: the seed among thorns never sprouts
it sprouts and grows, then gets slowly choked.
Jesus explains the parable to the twelve in private
alone with them, he explains it line by line.
Jesus taught this parable sitting in a boat

games.q: you're the seed, and you've sprouted among thorns. nobody has stepped on you and the sun hasn't burned you. what happens?
o: you grow into a great harvest.
the thorns grow up and slowly choke you.
games.why: "the cares of the world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts after other things entering in choke the word."

practice: Look back over the last few days: what choked the good things? Not a disaster, just the slow crowding, a worry you kept circling, money on your mind, wanting something so much it filled the room.
Name one thorn and see it clearly, without pulling it out yet; if you pray, show it to God, and if you don't, notice how much room it takes up.

wordCard.voice: The sower again. The parable of four kinds of ground, read now in Mark, with Jesus's own explanation beside it. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: thorns, the thistles and briars that choke the growing seed.

carryVoice: Your line: the thorns are the cares. Good ground still gives a hundredfold. Until tomorrow.
